title: ioctl_key_import: CRYPTO2DEV_KEY_SYMMETRIC not in valid key_type list
description: ioctl_key_import() validates key_type with: 'if (op.key_type \!= KEY_PRIVATE && op.key_type \!= KEY_PUBLIC && op.key_type \!= KEY_PAIR) return -EINVAL'. The UAPI header defines CRYPTO2DEV_KEY_PRIVATE=1, KEY_PUBLIC=2, KEY_PAIR=3. The DESIGN.md and UAPI docs state 'KEY fds are for asymmetric keys only. Symmetric keys (AES, HMAC, CMAC) are always supplied inline in INIT.' So there is no KEY_SYMMETRIC constant and symmetric key import via KEY fd is not supported — by design. The validation correctly rejects any key_type not in {1,2,3}. However: the internal state field is named 'key_type' and compared against the same constants in ioctl_do_sign (key_type == KEY_PUBLIC rejected) and ioctl_do_agree (same). These all work correctly. The UAPI comment for key_type in KEY_GET_INFO says 'CRYPTO2DEV_KEY_*' which is accurate. No bug — confirmed correct.
